summary: Proof-worth registry entries owned by agent-workspace.

entries.contract: Browser Observation Refs are generation-scoped exact pairs and canvas/native targets are state-free Locator queries.
entries.worth: This catches stale-state acceptance, ref aliasing, browser selector injection, and a third semantic handle model without native or browser side effects.
entries.guard: pure isolated state-root and schema checks; does not execute ./aos or require daemon, browser, native UI, or TCC

entries.contract: Browser routes emit typed Observation Refs, require original state for ref requests, reject selector-shaped refs, bind generation records to independently verified backend implementation closure, and fail before dispatch while atomic state/ref identity remains unproven.
entries.worth: This catches route-level regressions that pure generation tests cannot observe, including missing state forwarding and unreviewed backend admission.
entries.command: bash tests/browser/do-existing-verbs.test.sh && bash tests/browser/do-fill.test.sh && bash tests/browser/see-capture.test.sh && bash tests/browser/target-parser.test.sh && node --test tests/browser/runtime-resolver.test.mjs
entries.guard: direct Node wrappers, a fake native-capture primitive, package-backed fake Playwright, and a pure Swift parser harness only; does not execute ./aos, start the daemon, or access native UI/TCC

entries.contract: Session-only browser type and key remain available without state, every supplied state value is rejected before dispatch, and ref-bearing Observation Ref routes remain separately fail-closed.
entries.worth: This prevents the identity blocker from accidentally disabling existing session-only keyboard primitives or attaching false state provenance.
entries.guard: fake AOS version probe and fake Playwright executable only; does not execute ./aos or require daemon, browser, native UI, or TCC

entries.contract: V1 saved records contain one typed handle, V0 is byte-preserving fail-closed, state is accepted only for browser Observation Refs, and browser requests fail before dispatch while atomic state/ref identity remains unproven.
entries.worth: This is the atomic saved-workspace and fake-action regression boundary for the breaking V1 migration.
entries.guard: isolated state root and fake executables only; does not execute ./aos or require daemon, native UI, or TCC

entries.contract: Pending annotations project exactly one validated V1 saved handle without reviving resolution classes or alternate target identity.
entries.worth: This catches schema/model drift at the mechanically required pending-annotation projection boundary.
entries.guard: isolated local state and schema validation only; does not execute ./aos or require daemon/native UI/TCC

entries.contract: Canvas and native AX Locators reject zero and multiple matches; native index selects deterministically, near requires one unique closest bounded candidate, native NDJSON sessions reject state before dispatch, and AX capture emits only schema-valid Locator handles.
entries.worth: Pure Swift harnesses lock exact-one selection, session state admission, and native handle normalization independently of native UI and Accessibility permission.
entries.guard: Swift compile plus pure synthetic selection and encoding only; does not execute ./aos or access native UI/TCC

entries.contract: Gateway capture types expose state and handles, socket failures preserve target codes/details, SDK rejection preserves the same facts, and label-first clickElement is absent.
entries.worth: This proves the public gateway and SDK projection even when the package ts-node loader cannot start under the installed Node runtime.
entries.guard: TypeScript build plus pure local socket-envelope simulation; does not execute ./aos or access daemon/native UI/TCC

entries.contract: A live AOS canvas Locator re-resolves by canvas id and machine ref without state, rejects missing and disabled current targets mechanically, and dispatches one current unique target.
entries.worth: This is the maintained live acceptance proof that canvas Locators do not regain snapshot-state semantics after the V1 migration.
entries.guard: requires explicit live-runtime approval, a current native binary, the ready shared repo daemon, Screen Recording, and input permissions; serializes and mutates only harness-owned canvases; never run in static or default validation

entries.contract: Saved workspace schemas, compact refs, current installable skills, command manifests, and action ownership remain aligned.
entries.worth: This prevents current saved-workspace guidance and schema/action contracts from drifting after legacy skill cleanup.
entries.guard: static Node contract inspection; does not execute ./aos or require daemon/TCC
